options.text: The destination database where synced data lands
The SQL database where Synnduit stores its bookkeeping — mappings, transactions, value changes, and exceptions
The source system Synnduit reads from
The .NET library that contains the feeds and sinks

items.explanation: StarBridge is Synnduit's separate bookkeeping database — its memory of mappings, outcomes, change history, and errors.

misconceptions.a: The destination holds the synced data; StarBridge holds Synnduit's records about that data. They are separate databases.
misconceptions.c: Sources are external systems; StarBridge is internal to Synnduit.

items.stem: Which of the following does StarBridge store? (Select all that apply.)
items.explanation: All four. StarBridge records mappings, transactions (EntityTransaction), value changes (EntityValueChange), and exceptions (EntityException).

items.stem: How many StarBridge databases does a single Run use?

options.text: One shared across all Runs in the organization

items.explanation: There is one StarBridge database per Run. CSSD's Sync-SRC-DDH has three Runs, hence three StarBridge DBs.

misconceptions.b: Each Run gets its own StarBridge so its bookkeeping stays isolated.
misconceptions.c: A StarBridge DB covers a Run's whole set of entities, not one DB per entity type.

items.stem: You need to find, for one staff record, every field that changed and when. Which StarBridge table do you query?
items.explanation: EntityValueChange holds field-level diffs — which value changed, from what to what, and when.

misconceptions.c: EntityTransaction holds the per-record outcome, not the field-level diffs.
misconceptions.a: EntityException holds errors, not change history.

items.stem: Where do delta detection's "last run's recorded state" and a mapping physically live?
items.explanation: Both the recorded prior state (for diffing) and the source↔destination mappings are rows in StarBridge — that's what makes delta detection and non-duplication possible.
